sites.rationale: L8 explicitly states the FLAG tag was 'chimerized to the N-terminus of hD2', pinning insert_after_residue=0. DRD2 has no signal peptide (UniProt P14416); the topology landmarks confirm residues 1–35 are extracellular, placing the tag 35 residues from TM1 (starts at 36), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. Python confirmed residue_after = M (position 1). L9 and L11 independently confirm surface display and functional internalization of this FLAG-D2R construct. FLAG epitope chimerized to the N-terminus of full-length human D2R in pcDNA3.1+, with a three-amino-acid linker (EFT) between FLAG and hD2, retaining the start codon. Surface display confirmed by live-cell anti-FLAG antibody labeling of non-permeabilized neurons (DIV 11-12) and HEK293 cells.

sources.claim: The FLAG-hD 2 pcDNA3.1+ construct was generated by chimerizing the FLAG epitope to the N-terminus of hD 2 cDNA in pcDNA3.1+ (with the three amino acid linker sequence “EFT” between FLAG and hD 2 , and retaining the start codon of hD 2 ; cDNA Resource Centre ( www.cdna.org ), #DRD0200001). 3HA-hCB 1 pEF4 A and 3HA-hCB 2 pEF4A constructs have been described previously 19 54 .

In contrast, varicosities lacking such appositions, or contacting receptor-negative neurons, are largely quiescent, indicating that local interactions with receptor-expressing targets help specify dopamine release competence. To directly visualize receptor organization relative to release sites at endogenous expression levels, we generated ALFA-tag knock-in mice (ALFADoR mice) in which the N-termini of D1 and D2 dopamine receptors are epitope-tagged.
The N-terminal HA tag was shown to be well-tolerated by D2 dopamine receptors and enabled the detection of surface molecules [ 14 , 33 ].
The superecliptic pHluorin version of GFP was used to tag the D2 receptor because only membrane-bound receptors would be visible (the higher pH inside cells quenches the GFP).

literature_notes: All eleven ledger lines converge on a single junction: the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0) of DRD2. DRD2 is a class A GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks confirm residues 1–35 are extracellular, and TM1 begins at residue 36. Four distinct tags (FLAG, ALFA, HA, SEP/GFP) have been placed at this position in published full-length, membrane-anchored constructs. No ledger line pins any insertion in ECL1 (94–108), ECL2 (176–188), or ECL3 (399–409); those loops are not proposed. L10 mentions FLAG-, SEP-, and SNAP-tagged D2R constructs used for surface trafficking studies but does not explicitly state the tag position, so it was used only as corroborating context for the FLAG and SEP sites rather than as a primary anchor. The four sites reported are the same physical junction with different tags; they are reported separately because each is grounded in a distinct ledger line with a distinct tag type and distinct validation evidence, consistent with the instruction to report every site the ledger supports. ECL1 contains a conserved disulfide-forming C107 (paired with C182 in ECL2); ECL3 contains C399 and C401; these cysteines were noted as constraints that would apply to any internal site, but no ledger line supports an internal insertion so no internal sites are proposed.
